verdicts.lens: LOOK-AHEAD and timing: candle timestamp semantics/entry timing, act24 fill-timestamp leakage, hindsight (current) liquidity filter, one-event-per-2h rule, TP/SL intra-candle ordering

findings.issue: The 'liq >= $100k' filter uses CURRENT GeckoTerminal pool liquidity (pools_v3.json 'liq', discovered Sep 2026), i.e. a survivorship/hindsight filter applied to July-August events. It is the single input that creates the short-horizon edge.
findings.evidence: Among events passing the real-time-knowable filters (act24>=2 & prior1h<=0), the 34 events on tokens whose liquidity is NOW <$100k had comparable event-time activity (median prior-24h candle volume $450k-$2.4M per token, vs $999k median for the core set) but 1h net median -11.3% (29% positive) versus +4.8%/62% for the 65 'current-liquid' events. Replacing the hindsight filter with an event-time proxy (prior-24h candle volume >= $100k, any current liq) gives n=99: 1h net median 0.000 (51% positive), 4h +3.6% (56%), median-of-token-medians 1h -1.2% (12/24 tokens >0), 4h +6.2% (13/23). With v24>=$1M: 1h 0.0%, 4h 0.0%, 24h +11%. Only the 24h horizon retains a positive median (+21% n=84, 62%; 14/21 tokens >0; July-only same-token random baseline -2.6%).
findings.fix: Never filter on pools_v3 'liq'. Use an event-time liquidity proxy (prior-24h volume, or on-chain pool reserves/V3 liquidity at the event block via eth_getLogs) and compute the impact cost from that value too.
findings.effect_on_edge: 1h and 4h net edge collapses to ~0 (median 0.0%/+3.6%, ~50-56% win rate, token-median 1h negative). 24h median stays positive but on a small, clustered sample.

findings.issue: Leaderboard wallets (the act24 filter and the token universe) are selected with hindsight: the fomo leaderboards (24h/7d/30d/all) were pulled in early Sep 2026 and rank by realized PnL through Sep, and OHLCV was pulled only for the ~277 tokens most traded by those wallets (ordered by wallet count). Tokens these eventual winners were active in are conditionally more likely to have recovered from dips.
findings.evidence: pull_gt.py orders tokens by (prio, -w=number of leaderboard wallets, min_ts); 1309 RH tokens had >=2 leaderboard wallets filling but only 159 have >=30 candles; tokens WITH OHLCV have median current liq $133k vs $8k for those without. No point-in-time leaderboard exists in the data (fomoscope mirror is stale/bugged), so this cannot be corrected from the available files.
findings.fix: Reconstruct the wallet set as of each event date (e.g. wallets on the 30d leaderboard as of t) or use a fixed wallet set frozen before the backtest window; pull OHLCV for the full set of tokens those wallets traded, not the top-by-count subset.
findings.effect_on_edge: Unquantifiable here; biases both the act24 filter and the token universe toward survivors, so the remaining 24h edge is an upper bound.

findings.issue: TP+15% is filled off the candle HIGH; on an AMM there are no resting limit orders and a 15m wick can be a single sandwiched swap. Close-vs-high check shows a large share of TP hits are wick-only. The SL-first ordering in simulate() is already pessimistic (only 1 candle in the core set crossed both), so ordering is not the problem; the fill assumption is.
findings.evidence: Core set: 49 TP hits, 22 of them (45%) with candle close < +15%. Re-running with SL-first vs TP-first changes mean from +6.5% to +7.2% (immaterial). On the survivorship-free set (n=99), TP15/SL30/4h gives median +10.9%, 79% positive but MEAN only +3.0% per trade; SL30/24h mean is carried by outliers (median -0.4%, 48% positive).
findings.fix: Fill TP only when the candle close (or next candle open) is >= TP, or model a reactive exit at the next 1m close after the TP is crossed; report mean and sum, not just median, since the -30% stops dominate the tail.
findings.effect_on_edge: Reported '83% hit, median +11.8%, mean +6.5%' is optimistic on fills; realistic expectancy after removing the hindsight liq filter is ~+3% mean per trade with a heavy left tail.

findings.issue: 24h result is far less independent than n=65/n=99 suggests and is July-concentrated with outlier-driven means.
findings.evidence: Core 65 events collapse to 43 independent 24h clusters (57 4h clusters); the survivorship-free 24h set (n=84) has 55 clusters over 21 tokens; two tokens supply 24 of the events. Mean 24h net +48.8% falls to +35.7% excluding the top 3 trades (+328%, +440%, +441%). July: 62 events (median +28%, 56% positive) vs Aug 21 (median +12%, 76%). prior1h<=0 was one of several post-hoc subsets printed by the script (multiple-comparison).
findings.fix: Report cluster-level statistics (one observation per token per 24h window), a token-level sign test (14/21 positive, p~0.09 one-sided), and hold out August as a validation period for a rule chosen on July.
findings.effect_on_edge: 24h edge is suggestive, not established; statistical support is weak once clustering is accounted for.

findings.issue: Timing inputs that were checked and found clean (no correction needed): candle timestamps mark candle START (last candle ts 02:00 with file mtime 02:06, all ts%900==0), entry o[i+1] equals cl[i] in 98% of core events (median diff 0.000, max +0.2%), the one-event-per-2h rule is index-based and causal, and act24 uses fills in [t-24h, t) only; interpolated block timestamps (72% of RH fills) have leave-one-out error median 0.3s, p99 2.1s, so post-event fills cannot leak in. Excluding fills in the last hour before the crash changes act24>=2 status for only 3/65 core events.
findings.evidence: Direct recomputation from gt/ohlcv/*.json, rh/blocks/blocks*.json and rh/logs/*.ledger.json; 12/65 core events have a leaderboard fill DURING the crash candle, but these are not used by the act24 window.
findings.fix: None needed for these inputs.
findings.effect_on_edge: None.

verdicts.corrected_estimate: With the hindsight liquidity filter replaced by an event-time proxy (prior-24h volume >= $100k) and the same act24>=2 & prior1h<=0 filters, n=99 (24 tokens): 1h net median 0.0% (51% positive, token-median -1.2%); 4h net median +3.6% (56%); 24h net median ~+13% to +21% (57-62% positive, 14/21 tokens positive, ~55 independent clusters, mean driven by 3 outliers); TP+15%/SL-30%/4h mean ~+3% per trade (median +11%, 79% hit, but 45% of TP hits are wick-only). Short-horizon positive expectancy after costs is not supported; a 24h dip-buy edge remains suggestive but rests on hindsight-selected wallets/tokens and a small, July-heavy, clustered sample.
tests_run: Reproduced core set n=65 from crash_reversion_15m.json (liq>=100k & act24>=2 & prior1h<=0) and plain-exit nets (1h +4.8%/62%, 4h +4.1%/58%, 24h +24.6%/67%).
Verified GeckoTerminal candle timestamps mark candle start (ts%900==0; last candle 02:00 vs pull time 02:06) and that entry o[i+1]==cl[i] for 98% of events (max diff +0.2%).
Block-time interpolation leave-one-out error over 36,948 anchors: median 0.31s, p99 2.1s; recomputed act24 excluding fills in [t-1h,t): only 3/65 core events change status.
Split act24>=2&prior1h<=0 events by CURRENT liq: liq_now<100k (n=34) 1h net -11.3%/29% vs core +4.8%/62%; event-time prior-24h volume comparable across groups.

Re-ran all horizons with event-time volume proxy (v24>=100k/300k/1M, no current-liq filter): 1h net median 0.0%, 4h +3.6% to 0.0%, 24h +21% to +11%; token-median and leave-one-token-out stats; month split.
Random-entry baseline on the same survivorship-free tokens (all period and July-only): raw 24h median -1.5% / -2.6%, 1h -0.2%.

TP/SL simulate() audit: SL-first vs TP-first ordering (mean +6.5% vs +7.2%), both-crossed candles (1), wick-only TP hits (22/49), close-based TP variant; re-ran TP15/SL30/4h and SL30/24h on survivorship-free set (mean +3.0%; SL30/24h median -0.4%).
Independence: counted token-level 24h/4h clusters (65 -> 43/57; survivorship-free 84 -> 55 clusters, 21 tokens) and outlier contribution to 24h mean.

Universe selection: pull_gt.py orders OHLCV pulls by leaderboard-wallet count; 1309 RH tokens with >=2 wallets vs 159 with usable candles; tokens with OHLCV have median current liq $133k vs $8k without.

verdicts.lens: DATA ARTIFACTS: on-chain swap verification of GeckoTerminal 15m crash candles, candle alignment, wick dependence, and the validity of the 'liq' field used for impact costs

findings.issue: Two of the 64 Robinhood-chain core events are pure candle artifacts, and they are the two biggest candle 'winners'
findings.evidence: SPACEHOOD 08-27 16:30 (candle -39.0%, vol $2.4k, liq $1.96M) and 08-27 20:30 (candle -29.6%, vol $2.3k): exact Uniswap v4 swap prices in the same pool moved -0.6% and +3.2% over the candle. Candle x1h was +51.8% and +69.2%; swap x1h was -5.3% and +14.6%. Root cause: the token's GT candle pool is 'SPCX / SPACEHOOD' with base=False (SPACEHOOD is the quote side), and the price series flips bimodally between ~1.55e-3 and ~9.5e-4 on trivial volume. The third SPACEHOOD event is partially inflated (-20.3% candle vs -14.6% swaps). Pre-check flagged them: a $2.4k trade cannot move a $1.96M pool 39% (max ~0.5%). Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fomo-memebot/a7a59693-7c2d-5b6c-b7df-e43fdbe7d612/scratchpad/audit_swaps_15m.py, results audit_swaps_15m.json + audit_swaps_15m_b.json.
findings.fix: Drop tokens whose candle pool has base=False or whose quote is not WETH/USDG; require implied impact plausibility (|r| <= k * volume/liq) or verify every event against swap logs.
findings.effect_on_edge: Removes the two largest wins; 1h swap-based net median for the other 62 events is +5.1% under the claimed cost model, so the price signal itself survives this removal.

findings.issue: The other 62 crashes are real trades and the post-dip bounce is present on swap prices, so the bounce is NOT a candle artifact
findings.evidence: Swap-implied crash within 0.95pp (median) of the candle crash; candle timestamps confirmed start-aligned against swaps (FIRE 07-21 window, align_check.py); entry at first swap after t+900 is within +0.08% of the crash close. On swap prices with the claimed cost (2% + 2*500/(liq/2)): 1h net median +5.1%, 61% positive; 4h +4.1%, 60% positive. Note the claim's 'x1h' is close of candle i+5 = 75 min after entry, not 60.
findings.fix: None needed for the price path; keep in mind the 1h label is 75 min.
findings.effect_on_edge: No reduction from price artifacts beyond the SPACEHOOD events.

findings.issue: The 'liq' field is a data artifact for cost purposes: GT reserve-USD overstates effective depth 3-10x for these concentrated v3/v4 pools, so the impact term in the cost model is badly understated
findings.evidence: Measured from consecutive Swap logs (usd traded / |dln price|): $ needed to move price 1% is worth $231, FIRE $139, LIGER $150, YOLO $241, TENDIES $605, AI $1,376. One-way impact of a $500 order: 2.2%, 3.6%, 3.3%, 2.1%, 0.8%, 0.4% vs the model's 0.65%, 0.53%, 0.63%, 0.21%, 0.08%, 0.004%. Also FIRE moved -17% on $2.8k 'in a $188k pool' and was swap-confirmed real, i.e. the pool is far thinner than liq implies. impact_check.py.
findings.fix: Estimate impact from on-chain depth (sqrtPrice/L or empirical $ per 1%) rather than GT reserve USD; or restrict to pools with measured depth >= ~$1k per 1%.
findings.effect_on_edge: With measured impact (2% fee + 2x measured one-way impact, bucketed estimate for unmeasured tokens): 1h net median +1.6% (55% positive, mean +4.5%); 4h net median +0.1% (50% positive); Aug+ events 1h median -5.0% (48%); liq<$500k 1h median -5.0% (44%); the two dominant tokens worth (n=13) and LIGER (n=7) have 1h net medians -11.4% and -17.3%. TP15/SL30/4h on the swap path: median +6.7%, mean +0.7% (ambiguous TP&SL candles counted as SL) vs the claimed +11.8%/+6.5%. Only liq>=$500k (n=19) remains clearly positive: 1h net +8.0%, 79% positive.

findings.issue: Wick dependence of the TP+15% rule is minor
findings.evidence: Closes-only simulation on the same 65 events: TP hits 48 -> 43, SL 4 -> 2, net median unchanged at +11.8%, mean +6.7% -> +5.4%. On the swap path 46/62 events touch +15% and 6 touch -30% (4 touch both).
findings.fix: Report ambiguous-candle events conservatively (SL first).
findings.effect_on_edge: About -1pp on mean; not decisive.

findings.issue: Sparse trading in the crash candle and the Solana event are unverified
findings.evidence: 10 of 62 real events had fewer than 20 swaps in the crash candle; the single Solana event (Ge87...pump) could not be verified with the EVM method.
findings.fix: Require a minimum swap count in the crash candle; verify Solana via Helius transactions.
findings.effect_on_edge: Small; the candle-vs-swap agreement is still good on these events.

verdicts.corrected_estimate: 62/64 Robinhood events are real crashes; 2 (both SPACEHOOD 08-27, the two largest candle winners) are artifacts. On swap prices with realistic, measured impact the strategy is roughly break-even: 1h net median ~+1.5% (55% positive), 4h net ~0% (50% positive), Aug+ negative (-5% 1h median), TP15/SL30/4h mean ~+1% to +4% (vs claimed +6.5%). Positive expectancy survives only in the liq>=$500k subset (n=19, 1h net ~+8%, ~79% positive), which is too small and July-heavy to support the general claim.
tests_run: Reconstructed the 65 core events from crash_reversion_15m.json (liq>=100k, act24>=2, prior1h<=0): 64 Robinhood + 1 Solana, 15 tokens
Physical plausibility pre-screen: max constant-product drop given candle volume vs GT liq flagged 14 suspect events (SPACEHOOD, AI, YOLO, FIRE, Index)

Fetched exact Uniswap v3/v4 Swap logs via rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com for all 64 RH events over [prev candle close, entry+4h], with exact block<->timestamp resolution via eth_getBlockByNumber; recomputed crash, 1h/4h returns, max/min path (audit_swaps_15m.py, _b shard)
Candle timestamp alignment test on FIRE 07-21: start-aligned candle returns match swap returns candle by candle; end-aligned do not
Quote-token conversion inspection: SPCX/USDG and NVDA/USDG candles around SPACEHOOD and AI events; NVDA series oscillates ~5% candle to candle, SPACEHOOD prints bimodally
Effective depth measurement from swap logs ($ per 1% price move) for worth, FIRE, LIGER, YOLO, TENDIES, AI vs GT liq-based impact model (impact_check.py)
Swap-based net return tables under claimed vs measured cost models, by token, month, and liq bucket; TP15/SL30/4h on swap path with conservative and optimistic ambiguity handling (audit_final.py)
Wick dependence test of TP/SL rule using candle highs/lows vs closes only

verdicts.lens: Survivorship / universe selection (hindsight-selected token universe, look-ahead liquidity filter, right-censored and gapped returns, hindsight-free re-test)

findings.issue: The 'pool liquidity >= $100k' filter uses CURRENT liquidity (reserve_in_usd snapshotted Sep 4 in gt/pools_v3.json), not liquidity at event time. It is a look-ahead survivorship filter: it keeps only tokens whose pools were still deep on Sep 4, i.e. tokens that survived after the dip.
findings.evidence: crash_reversion_15m.py reads liq from d['pool']['liq'] which gt_common.py fills from GeckoTerminal reserve_in_usd at fetch time (no history). Same events, act24>=2 & prior1h<=0, split by current liq: liq now >=100k (the 65 'core' events): 1h net med +4.8%, p>0 0.62; liq now 10k-100k (33 events): 1h net med -11.3%, p>0 0.29, TPSL mean -3.2%. Removing the filter (n=99): 1h net med +0.0%, p>0 0.51. On today's larger candle set (299 core events / 72 tokens): with filter 1h +5.0%, without filter +2.7% (p>0 0.56); on pooled RH data tokens now at 10k-100k liq: 1h med -5.4%, 24h med -17.2%.
findings.fix: Replace current-liq with an event-time proxy (prior-24h candle $volume, or archived reserve snapshots) and never filter on end-of-sample state; report results without any post-hoc liquidity gate.
findings.effect_on_edge: 1h edge falls from +4.8%/+6.5% to ~0 to +2.7% net; 24h and TP/SL edges shrink by roughly half.

findings.issue: Token universe is doubly hindsight-selected: (i) only tokens traded by TODAY's leaderboard traders were candle-fetched, prioritised by their closed trades and by >=3-wallet fill demand; (ii) the act24 gate is evaluated with wallets that are winners as of Sep 4, not wallets that were on the board at event time.
findings.evidence: From the ledgers, 1,930 tokens had >=2 leaderboard wallets fill within a 24h window ('socially active'), but only 188 (10%) have candles in gt/ohlcv. Tokens with candles have median 9.5 distinct leaderboard wallets vs 3.0 for those without; of the 1,742 uncovered socially-active tokens, 852 are unknown to GeckoTerminal (no pool) and 373 have <$10k liquidity today, vs only 25/269 (9%) of the candle universe. A hindsight-free universe (tokens held by >=2 traders on the fomoscope boards of Aug 27-29) has 36% of tokens at <$10k liquidity today and median liq $19k, vs 58% >=100k in the candle universe. The act24 gate itself adds little in-universe (act24<2 events: 1h +3.7%, TPSL 73%), i.e. the 'social' signal is not what drives the result.
findings.fix: Build the universe from information available at event time (leaderboard snapshots at t, positions captured before t, live ws_alerts) and fetch candles for the full socially-active set including tokens that later died.
findings.effect_on_edge: The backtest is run on ~10% of the eligible universe, the surviving/most-active tail; expectancy on the full universe is unknown from the claim's data and negative on the hindsight-free re-test below.

findings.issue: Hindsight-free re-test is negative. Universe built from fomoscope leaderboards captured Aug 27-29 (485 traders) -> their positions captured <=Aug 29 -> tokens held by >=2 of them (255 Solana mints; 81 fetched). Dip test on out-of-sample events (>= Aug 30) shows dip-buying loses.
findings.evidence: OOS crash events n=76 (33 tokens): 1h net med -8.7% (p>0 0.34), 4h -9.6%, 24h -18.3%, TPSL med -2.1% mean -5.7% (48% positive). With prior1h<=0 and event-time vol24>=250k (n=23): 1h -5.5%, 4h -6.3%, 24h -15.1%, TPSL mean -5.3%. With act24>=2 over the whole period (n=57): 1h -10.0%, 24h -47.8%, TPSL mean -7.4%. Random baseline on the same tokens: 1h -1.5%, 4h -1.6%, 24h -14.1% (drift explains only part; the dip entries underperform even that). Caveat: this universe is Solana, whereas the claim's core is ~all Robinhood-chain (352/353 core events); a Robinhood hindsight-free sample was started (gt/ohlcv_soc, 9 tokens so far) and its early events are also negative (n=5 prior<=0/act24>=2: 1h -13%, 24h -14%) but the sample is too small to be conclusive.
findings.fix: Re-run the Robinhood-chain test on the full socially-active set once the soc_fetch.py pull finishes (gt/ohlcv_soc), and require out-of-sample time windows relative to the universe-selection date.
findings.effect_on_edge: Sign flips from positive to negative on a universe selected without hindsight.

findings.issue: Missing 4h/24h returns are silently dropped. In the 65-event set 10/65 (15%) of 24h returns are missing; in the current 299-event set 62/293 are missing (26 right-censored by series end on Sep 4, 36 due to candle gaps = no trades for >=15m after a crash, i.e. illiquid periods).
findings.evidence: Claim 24h net med +24.6% (n=55). Filling missing with -100%: median +6.1%, mean +39%, p>0 0.57 (65-set); on 299-set: -2.0% median, p>0 0.48. Filling with next-available candle (fair for gaps): +23.1% (65-set) / +14.1% uncensored (299-set); the gapped events themselves have next-available 24h return median +6.5%, p>0 0.53. Only 2/74 core tokens are now <10% of ATH and 6/299 events never regained entry, so in-universe death is rare — because the universe was selected for survival (see finding 2).
findings.fix: Report 24h stats with censored events excluded and gaps filled with next-available price; never drop missing outcomes.
findings.effect_on_edge: 24h median between -2% and +14% depending on treatment, not +23-25%.

findings.issue: Effective sample size is small and clustered; the claimed n=65 comes from a stale candle snapshot. The candle universe was re-pulled after the analysis (files timestamped 06:43-06:49 Sep 4 vs crash_reversion_15m.py at 02:43), so the current data gives 299 core events over 72 tokens (Jul 66 / Aug 146 / Sep 84), not 65 over 15 with 42 in July.
findings.evidence: In the 65-set, 2 tokens contribute 23 events; per-token medians: 10/15 tokens positive at 1h, median of token medians +6.0%; 0xfb1bcb (13 events) 1h med -4.8%, 24h -13.6%. Overlapping 24h holds on the same token make events non-independent. On the 299-set, 64% of tokens have positive 1h median, median of token TPSL means +9.7%; by month July is weakest (1h +2.0%, 24h +1.6%).
findings.fix: Report per-token (cluster) statistics and refresh the event set on the current candle files; treat July (42 of 65) as one regime.
findings.effect_on_edge: Point estimates unstable; the in-universe result does replicate on the larger set (1h +5%, TPSL 82%), but that set carries the same survivorship filters.

findings.issue: Random-entry baseline per token does not explain the in-universe result, so survivorship of the universe (not token drift) is the operative bias.
findings.evidence: Matched random entries on the same token within +-3 days of each core event: 1h/4h/24h medians -0.0%/-0.2%/+4.2% (means -0.1%/-0.2%/+15%); core excess over matched baseline +7.5% (1h) and +17.8% (24h). The pooled RH sample by current-liq bucket shows the mechanism directly: liq now >=100k 1h +4.0%, 10k-100k -5.4%, <10k -60%.
findings.fix: Use the baseline as a control but recognise it is computed on the same survivor universe; the correct control is the hindsight-free universe.
findings.effect_on_edge: Confirms the reported edge is conditional on the token having survived to Sep 4.

verdicts.corrected_estimate: On the claim's own (survivor) universe with only event-time filters (prior1h<=0, act24>=2, prior-24h volume >= $250k, no current-liquidity gate): 1h net median about +1.6% to +2.4% (p>0 0.54-0.56), 4h +4%, 24h about +2% (gaps filled, censored excluded) and -5% if missing = -100%; TP+15/SL-30/4h mean +2.5% to +3.4% (77% hit) using the optimistic wick-fill assumption. On a hindsight-free universe (tokens held by >=2 traders on the Aug 27-29 leaderboards, tested Aug 30-Sep 4, Solana): 1h net median -5.5% to -8.7%, 24h -15% to -18%, TP/SL mean -5%, i.e. negative expectancy. The claimed +6.5%/+22.8%/+11.8% figures are an artefact of filtering on Sep-4 liquidity and of a universe restricted to ~10% of socially-active tokens (the most-traded survivors); the positive-expectancy claim is not supported once that selection is removed. Best corrected point estimate: roughly zero to slightly negative after costs, with a residual in-sample TP/SL edge of ~+2-3% that has not been shown to survive on an unselected universe.
tests_run: Reproduced core event set from crash_reversion_15m.json (n=65: 1h net med +4.8%, 24h +24.6% n=55, TPSL med +11.8% mean +6.4%) and re-generated events from the current candle files (audit_dip.py: 299 core events / 72 tokens)
Traced 'liq' to gt_common.py reserve_in_usd at fetch time (Sep 4 snapshot) and split events by current-liq bucket with and without the filter
Event-time liquidity proxy (prior-24h candle $ volume at 50k-1M thresholds) instead of current liq
Missing 4h/24h returns decomposed into right-censoring vs candle gaps; recomputed with -100% fill and next-available-candle fill
TP/SL simulation re-implemented; variants: SL gap-aware fill, TP on close; ambiguity check (both levels touched in one candle: 3/256)
Per-token cluster statistics, month split, exclusion of the two heaviest tokens
Matched random-entry baseline per token (+-3 days around each event, 20 draws) and excess over baseline

Universe survivorship census: 269 candle tokens vs 1,930 socially-active tokens from rh/logs + helius ledgers; current liq and drawdown-from-ATH distributions; fomoscope hindsight-free universe liquidity distribution (36% <$10k)

Built hindsight-free universe from fomoscope leaderboards/positions captured <= Aug 29 (255 tokens, 81 fetched from GeckoTerminal) and ran the dip test out-of-sample (>= Aug 30) with all filter variants and a random baseline

Started a random-sample fetch of Robinhood socially-active tokens absent from the claim universe (gt/ohlcv_soc, 9/75 tokens fetched at report time) and ran the dip test on the partial sample plus pooled-by-current-liq analysis
Confirmed the claim's core is ~100% Robinhood chain (352/353 events) and that in-universe Solana events (n=39, no liq gate) are flat-to-negative at 1h

verdicts.lens: Costs and executability for a retail trader (fees, creator/hook taxes, event-time depth/impact, latency, stop-loss gap risk, gas)

findings.issue: The cost model's price-impact term understates real event-time impact by ~4-6x. GeckoTerminal 'liq' (and it is the CURRENT Sep-3 reserve, not event-time) implies ~$940/1% move for FIRE ($188k) and $800/1% for LIGER; swap-log depth at the events is $124-462/1% (FIRE) and $128-544/1% (LIGER). Median model-depth/empirical-depth ratio = 5.9 (p25 3.3) across 28 swap-verified events.
findings.evidence: exec_audit.py / exec_audit.json (USD per 1% log move from consecutive v3/v4 Swap events in [t-1h,t+4h]); prior impact_check.py gave same picture (worth 2.2%, FIRE 3.6%, LIGER 3.3% one-way for $500). Crash-candle volume median $18k, 18/65 events < $10k; max single swap in crash candle often $0.5-5k, i.e. a $500-5k clip is a large fraction of the market.
findings.fix: Use swap-derived depth (or DexScreener 'liquidity' divided by ~5) and size clips at <=2% of event-time depth; recompute net with round-trip impact ≈ size/depth.
findings.effect_on_edge: $500 clip: TP15/SL30/4h net median falls from +11.9% (claim model) to +9.2% with realistic fees+impact+60s reaction (mean +5.4%); $2,000 clip: median +2.9%, mean -0.4%; $5,000 clip: median -7.7%, mean -12%, p>0 36%. The strategy is capacity-limited to a few hundred dollars per event.

findings.issue: Fee schedule in the claim (2% round trip) is wrong for the app path and pool-specific fees were not checked. On-chain: fomo app 0.5%/side + pool fee 1% (Pons V1 v3 pools: LIGER, wire, Index, JUGGERNAUT, worth, MARIAN, WISHBONE, TENDIES, YOLO), 0.3% (CASHCAT, FIRE), 0.35% (PONS), 0.7% dynamic fee via LONG hook 0x4e34...a544 (AI, SPACEHOOD) -> app path round trip = 3% for most tokens, not 2%. AI and SPACEHOOD are quoted in tokenized stocks (NVDA, SPCX) so a retail buyer needs an extra hop each way (extra fee + impact). Pons V2 maxCreatorTaxBps=1000 (10%) exists on-chain but none of the 15 event tokens is registered with the V2 hook, so no creator tax applied to this set; the v4 hook fee (100 bps) applies to both legs of V2-launched tokens, which would matter for any future universe.
findings.evidence: readpons.py + eth_call getLaunchedToken/launches; pool fee() on v3 pools; Uniswap v4 Swap event 'fee' field decoded (AI 7000, SPACEHOOD 7000, FIRE 3000, PONS 3499 pips); docs.ponsfamily.com ('Pool fee: 10000 (1%)', 70/30 creator/protocol split, applies to buys and sells); KuCoin write-up: LONG '~13%' platform fees (unverified, only 0.7% visible in swap fee field).
findings.fix: Model fees per pool: 2*(0.5%+pool_fee)+hop costs; for future tokens read creatorTaxBps/hookFeeBps from the V2 hook before trading.
findings.effect_on_edge: Adds ~1 pp round-trip vs the claim for 9 of 15 tokens and ~1-1.5 pp for AI/SPACEHOOD (9 events).

findings.issue: Stop-loss fills cannot be guaranteed on-chain; gap risk is real but modest in this sample. Of 28 swap-verified events, 3 triggered -30%: FIRE 07-20 triggered at -30.4% and the next swap filled at -40.3% (10-pt gap); FIRE 08-25 -32.2%->-33.0%; LIGER 08-31 -33.8%->-30.8%. Take-profit +15% is likewise not a resting order; a poller sells at the next swap (I used first-swap-after-trigger for both legs).
findings.evidence: exec_audit.json 'stop'/'tp' fields (trig, fill_next_swap, min_next60s). Candle-level check (audit): 6/65 events cross -30% intracandle.
findings.fix: Simulate stop/TP fills at the first observable swap after trigger plus impact; do not assume level fills.
findings.effect_on_edge: Mean net for TP/SL rule drops ~1 pp relative to level-fills; tail loss per stopped trade is -33% to -40% instead of -30%.

findings.issue: Detection latency: a human on the fomo app cannot see or act on a 15m -15% candle within a candle; the app feed carries only buy/sell/thesis/perp alerts, no price-drop alerts. A scripted 30s DexScreener poll can; reaction cost measured on swap path: +60s median 0.0% (mean -0.3%), +120s +0.2%, +300s +1.9% (54% of events already >1% higher), +600s +6.0%, +900s +7.4%.
findings.evidence: exec_audit.json 'lat' (first swap price at entry+N s vs first swap after candle close); fapi/ws_alerts.jsonl alertType counts (buy/sell/thesis/perp/alert only). Candle test: entering one candle late cuts gross TP/SL median from +13.5% to +8.9% and mean from +15% to +5%.
findings.fix: Only viable as an automated bot with <=2 min reaction; retail manual execution should be modelled at +5-15 min.
findings.effect_on_edge: 5-min reaction: $500 net median +6.9%, mean +3.2%, p>0 75%; $2k: median 0.0%, mean -2.6%. 15-min (manual) reaction removes most of the rebound.

findings.issue: Gas is not the binding cost. fomo fills are ERC-4337 bundled (0x4337... bundlers, 0.46-2.5M gas, median ~1.0M) and sponsored; direct on-chain at event blocks cost median $0.26 round trip (max $3) at 0.02-0.63 gwei and ETH ~$2.4k. Hourly baseFee samples Aug30-Sep3 peaked 1.36 gwei (Sep 3 15:17) and 1.26 gwei (Sep 2 15:29) -> ~$3-7 per 1M-gas swap; intra-hour spikes to the $20-60 reported were not captured by hourly sampling but would be 4-12% of a $500 clip per leg if hit.
findings.evidence: eth_getTransactionReceipt on 12 recent leaderboard fills; basefee_series.json (eth_getBlockByNumber hourly); exec_audit gas fields.
findings.fix: Add a gas guard (skip direct-on-chain entries when baseFee > ~2 gwei with a $500 clip); irrelevant on the sponsored app path.
findings.effect_on_edge: <0.1 pp normally; up to -10 to -25 pp per trade in congestion spikes for small clips.

findings.issue: Concentration and regime: 28-event swap-verified subset is 10 FIRE + 7 LIGER + 6 AI; full set has worth+FIRE = 23/65 events and the prior swap-level audit found per-token 1h net(emp) negative for worth (n=13, med -11%), LIGER (-17%), FIRE (-2%), YOLO (-3%). July vs Aug+ with realistic $500/60s TP/SL is similar (med +9.1% vs +9.3%) but 1h/4h close exits in Aug+ with empirical impact were negative in the prior audit (1h net(emp) med -5.0%, 4h -1.4%). Under a 3x lower-activity regime (depth/3): $500 clip median +5.4% but mean +1.5% (Aug+ mean +0.9%); $2,000 clip median -11% to -17%, p>0 13-25%.
findings.evidence: final_net.py on exec_audit.json (n=28, run was 28/64 complete at report time); audit_final.py per-token table.
findings.fix: Report per-token and per-month results; cap size at ~$500 and require depth >= $1,000/1% at signal time.
findings.effect_on_edge: Positive expectancy survives only for a ~$500 automated clip; any regime with 3x thinner books or clips >= $2k is negative.

verdicts.corrected_estimate: Swap-path verified subset (n=28 of 64 RH events; run still completing), TP+15%/SL-30%/4h, fills at first swap after trigger, fees = 2*(0.5% app + on-chain pool fee) + stock-hop for AI/SPACEHOOD, impact = size / empirical event-time depth, 60s reaction: $500 clip net median +9.2%, mean +5.4%, p>0 82% (vs claim +11.8%/+6.5%); $2,000 clip median +2.9%, mean -0.4%, p>0 64%; $5,000 clip median -7.7%, mean -12%, p>0 36%. 1h-close exit $500: median +3.4%, mean +2.6%, p>0 61%; 4h-close: median +0.6%, mean +7.4%, p>0 50%. With 5-min manual reaction: $500 median +6.9%, mean +3.2%; $2k median 0.0%. Under 3x lower activity (depth/3): $500 median +5.4%, mean +1.5% (Aug+ mean +0.9%); $2,000 median -11% to -17%, p>0 13-25%. Gas negligible on the sponsored app path (~$0.3 round trip direct on-chain normally; $20-60/tx spikes would be -4 to -12% per leg on $500). Conclusion: the claim of positive expectancy 'after costs' holds only for an automated (<2 min) ~$500 clip on the same 3-4 tokens; it is capacity-limited to a few hundred dollars per event, not robust to clip size, thinner books, or manual execution, and the prior audit's 1h/4h close-exit versions are ~0 to negative with empirical impact in Aug+. Refuted as a general retail edge.

verdicts.lens: STATISTICS and REGIME (clustered inference, multiple testing, out-of-sample stability, mirror/generic mean-reversion)

findings.issue: Headline numbers on the n=65 core set are not statistically established once clustering is respected; several quoted figures also do not reproduce from the saved event file.
findings.evidence: Reproduced from crash_reversion_15m.json (liq>=100k, prior1h<=0, act24>=2 -> n=65, 15 tokens, 64/65 Robinhood): net 1h median is +4.8% (62% positive), not +6.5%. Token-clustered bootstrap 95% CI of the net median: 1h [-0.2%, +10.8%], 4h [-1.4%, +15.0%]; day-clustered 1h [-0.1%, +9.9%], 4h [-0.5%, +14.5%]. Sign test on token-level medians: 1h 10/15 positive (p=0.15), 4h 8/15 (p=0.50). Only the means (1h [+2.6%, +17.6%]) and the 24h horizon ([+1.7%, +61.5%], but with 10/65 events dropped as missing) are clear of zero. 22/65 events start within 24h of a same-token event, 9/65 within 4h, so the 4h/24h windows overlap.
findings.fix: Report token- and day-clustered CIs and the sign test on token medians; quote the reproducible +4.8% net 1h median; treat 4h/24h numbers as overlapping observations.
findings.effect_on_edge: On the claim's own 65 events the after-cost median at 1h/4h is not distinguishable from zero; the evidence there rests on a right-skewed mean.

findings.issue: The TP+15%/SL-30%/4h summary ('83% hit, median +11.8%') is mechanically uninformative: it reproduces under random entries on the same tokens.
findings.evidence: Permutation null (same events, forward returns drawn from random candles of the same token): the claim-combo TP/SL median has a null 95th percentile of +11.7% vs observed +11.8%, and on the ±3-day time-matched null the mean TP/SL median is +8.8% on the claim set and +11.4% on the full set. Because the rule's outcome is +15%−cost whenever the hit rate exceeds 50%, the median is ~+12% for any set with hit>50%. What does beat the null is the TP/SL mean: +6.4% vs null [-5.2%, +2.7%] (p<0.001, claim set) and +5.1% vs [-4.5%, -0.8%] (full set). Hit rate 80% vs null 58%.
findings.fix: Report only the TP/SL mean (and its clustered CI); drop the 'median +11.8%' figure. Note that the TP fill is assumed at the level when a 15m candle high touches it (wick fills), which inflates the mean.
findings.effect_on_edge: The most quoted exit-rule statistic carries no information about edge; the informative quantity is a mean of +3% to +6% per trade with a token-clustered CI of [+3.4%, +6.6%] on the full set, dependent on wick-fill assumptions.

findings.issue: Multiple-testing exposure is large; the reported 'core' combination is one of a grid of ~360 filter/horizon/exit combinations, of which 208/246 (with n>=15) have a positive net median, and further universes/variants were examined outside the grid.
findings.evidence: Grid: crash thr {-15,-20,-25} x prior1h {any,<=0,>0} x liq {100k,500k} x act24 {0,1,2,3} x exits {15m,1h,4h,24h,TP/SL} = 360; 246 have n>=15; best-of-grid medians reach +66% (24h) and +44% (4h). Additional analyses in the scratchpad: 48 rep() subset reports across crash_reversion_15m.py/audit_dip.py/audit_new.py/crash_swaps.py, a 1-minute variant (crash_reversion_1m.json, 285 events), two extra universes (ohlcv_hf, ohlcv_soc), vol24>=250k filters, and missing-exit fill variants. Against a max-of-grid null the claim combo's median survives at 1h (p=0.017) and 15m (p<0.001) but not at 4h (p=0.19) or 24h (p=0.11); the claim combo's mean does not beat the max-of-grid null at any close-exit horizon (p=0.15-0.86).
findings.fix: Pre-register one rule (the 15m/1h close-to-close or TP/SL mean) and evaluate it on data collected after 2026-09-03; report the grid-adjusted p-values.
findings.effect_on_edge: The 4h and 24h claims (+4.0%, +22.8%) are consistent with selection from a large grid on right-skewed tokens; the short-horizon (15m-1h) reversal is the only part robust to grid selection.

findings.issue: The edge is generic short-horizon overreaction after any sharp candle in these AMM memecoins, symmetric in both directions; the 'socially-active' and 'prior1h<=0' filters add nothing, and most of the bounce is realised in the first 15 minutes, so it is execution-fragile.
findings.evidence: Mirror: pumps >=+15% (act24>=2, n=1008, 100 tokens) show raw 1h median -3.3%, 4h -4.5%, 15m -1.5% (42-44% positive); pumps >=+50% show -13% at 1h. Lag-1 autocorrelation of 15m log returns across all 520k candles of liq>=100k tokens is -0.034 (-0.040 for vol>=2k). Conditional on any 15m candle <-15% (n=3134, no filters at all), the next 15m return has median +2.1%, mean +3.6%; dose-response is monotone from -5% dips (+1.0%) to -35% dips (+20%). On the 183 core dips the 15m return is 76% of the 1h median; entering one candle late gives net median -2.2% (40% positive). Close-at-low crash candles (79/183) show a raw 15m median of -1.0%, i.e. when the last print is the extreme, the immediate bounce is absent. Report itself notes dips without leaderboard fills bounce equally (n=247). In exact swap data the net return at 60 s is -2.2% (31% positive): there is no instantaneous bid-ask bounce to capture; the reversal builds over 5-15 minutes.
findings.fix: Frame the strategy as 'buy any >=15% 15-minute drop in a liquid pool and exit within 15-60 minutes', drop the social filters, and require execution within ~1-2 minutes of the candle close; measure the raw 15m reversal (+2% to +4%) against total round-trip cost.
findings.effect_on_edge: Raw 15-minute reversal of roughly +2% to +4% median is of the same order as the 2% assumed round-trip cost; with any additional creator tax or slippage the median is at or below zero.

findings.issue: Out-of-sample stability is mixed: an expanded universe of new tokens is positive, but the only strictly post-claim events are negative, the exact-swap verification is not significant at the median, and the universe is still selected on current (lookahead) liquidity.
findings.evidence: (i) 276 core events on 71 tokens absent from the claim file (Jul-Sep 3): net 1h median +4.2% (62%), 4h +6.6%, TP/SL mean +5.3%, token-clustered CIs 1h [+1.5%, +6.1%], TP/SL mean [+2.7%, +6.6%]; 45/53 trading days positive; ICC by token 0.04-0.15 (effective n ~250-315 of 356). (ii) The 15 events after the claim's last timestamp (Sep 3 19:15 - Sep 4 05:30, 13 tokens): net 1h median -7.3% (33% positive), TP/SL mean -3.6%, hit 53%. (iii) July core events in the expanded set: 1h median +1.5%, 4h +2.5%, 24h -0.4% (48% positive) vs the claim file's July +7.5%/+8.9%/+39%; weeks of Jul-20, Jul-27 and Aug-10 have negative or ~zero 1h medians. (iv) Solana liq>=100k dips (n=24): 1h median -0.1%, TP/SL mean +0.1%, hit 58% - the effect is Robinhood-only. (v) Exact swaps (137 events, 136 in September, 37 tokens): net 30m median +1.8% with token-clustered CI [-3.6%, +7.2%]; mean +10.3% [+0.7%, +21.6%]; breakeven round-trip cost for the median is 4.7%, and at a 4% fee the median is -0.2%. (vi) Removing the current-liquidity lookahead (event-time vol24>=250k, all current liq): 1h median +1.5% (53% positive), TP/SL mean +2.0%; the events in tokens whose liquidity later fell below 100k (n=157) have 1h median -6.2% and TP/SL mean -4.2%, so the liq>=100k filter selects survivors. Counting missing 24h exits as -100% turns the 24h median to -3.3% (core) and -10.3% (no lookahead).
findings.fix: Run the rule forward on live data with a fixed universe rule using event-time liquidity; treat 24h returns as undefined until dead tokens are counted; separate Robinhood from Solana.
findings.effect_on_edge: Honest per-trade expectancy shrinks from the claimed +6.5%/+22.8% medians to a 30-60 minute median of about -1% to +4% at 2% costs (~0 at 4-5%), with a positive but fragile mean of +2% to +5% carried by the right tail.

verdicts.corrected_estimate: Robinhood-chain 15m dips >=15% in pools currently >=$100k: net per-trade expectancy at 30-60 min has a median of roughly -1% to +4% (central ~+2%) assuming a 2% round trip, falling to about 0% or below if the true round trip is 4-5% (untested Pons creator taxes); the mean under TP15/SL30/4h is +2% to +5% (token-clustered CI [+3%, +7%] on the full survivor-selected set, [+0%, +3%] without the current-liquidity lookahead, and dependent on wick-level TP fills). The claim's 65-event medians (+6.5% 1h, +22.8% 24h) are not reproducible/robust: 1h/4h clustered CIs include zero, 24h flips negative when missing exits are counted at -100%, the TP/SL median is a mechanical artifact, the post-claim 15 events are negative, Solana shows nothing, and the effect is generic symmetric overreaction (pumps revert equally) concentrated in the first 15 minutes rather than a social-activity edge.

conclusion:
# Audit conclusion: "Buy sharp dips in liquid, socially-active memecoins"

**Verdict in one line: refuted as stated. The headline numbers are an artifact of a hindsight liquidity filter, a survivor-selected token universe, two bogus candles, and a cost model that understates impact 4-6x. What survives is a generic, latency-critical 15-minute overreaction bounce worth roughly +1% to +3% mean per trade on a ~$500 clip, with a confidence interval that includes zero once you remove the lookahead. That is not a retail-executable edge.**

All five auditors independently refuted the claim (1 fatal, 4 material). Their findings agree on mechanism and largely on magnitude.

---

## 1. Findings by severity

### Fatal (each alone invalidates the claim as stated)

| # | Finding | Evidence | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **`liq >= $100k` is current (Sep-4) liquidity, not event-time liquidity.** It is a survivorship filter applied to July-August events: it keeps only tokens whose pools were still deep a month later. | `gt_common.py` fills `liq` from GeckoTerminal `reserve_in_usd` at fetch time; no history. Same events, same act24/prior1h filters, split by current liq: liq-now >= $100k (the 65 "core") 1h net +4.8%/62% positive; liq-now $10k-100k (n=33-34) 1h net **-11.3%/29%**; pooled RH by bucket: >= $100k +4.0%, $10k-100k -5.4%, < $10k -60%. Event-time activity of the two groups was comparable. | Replacing with event-time proxy (prior-24h volume >= $100k-250k): 1h median 0.0% to +2.4% (51-56% positive), token-median 1h negative, TP/SL mean +2.0% to +3.4%. The 1h/4h edge collapses. |
| F2 | **Token universe and wallet set are hindsight-selected.** Leaderboards pulled Sep 2026 rank by realized PnL through Sep; OHLCV was pulled only for the ~10% of socially-active tokens most traded by those eventual winners. | 1,930 tokens had >= 2 leaderboard wallets fill in a 24h window; 188 have candles. Tokens with candles: median current liq $133k; without: $8k. 852 uncovered tokens are unknown to GeckoTerminal (dead). Hindsight-free universe (fomoscope boards Aug 27-29, tested Aug 30-Sep 4, Solana, n=76): 1h net **-8.7%**, 4h -9.6%, 24h -18.3%, TP/SL mean -5.7%, worse than the random baseline on the same tokens. RH hindsight-free sample (n=5, too small) also negative. | Sign of the edge flips on an unselected universe. Cannot be corrected from existing files; needs point-in-time universes. |

### Material (each moves the estimate by >= 1-3 pp or invalidates a quoted statistic)

| # | Finding | Evidence | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **Two of the 64 RH events are candle artifacts, and they are the two largest winners.** SPACEHOOD 08-27 16:30 and 20:30: candle -39%/-30% on $2.4k volume in a $1.96M pool (physically impossible); exact v4 swaps moved -0.6%/+3.2%. Candle 1h +52%/+69%; swap 1h -5%/+15%. Cause: GT candle pool is SPCX/SPACEHOOD with `base=False`, prints bimodally. | `audit_swaps_15m.py` | Removes the top two wins; 62 remaining crashes are real (swap-confirmed). |
| M2 | **Impact term understated 4-6x.** GT reserve-USD overstates effective depth of concentrated v3/v4 pools. Measured $ per 1% move: worth $231, FIRE $139, LIGER $150, YOLO $241, TENDIES $605, AI $1,376 vs model-implied $800-$940+. Median model/empirical depth ratio 5.9. | `impact_check.py`, `exec_audit.py` (28 swap-verified events) | With measured impact: 1h net median +1.6% (55%), 4h +0.1% (50%), Aug+ 1h -5.0% (48%). worth (n=13) and LIGER (n=7) 1h net -11%/-17%. Strategy is capacity-limited to ~$500/event. |
| M3 | **Fees are 3% round trip, not 2%.** fomo app 0.5%/side + pool fee 1% (Pons V1 pools: 9 of 15 tokens), 0.3-0.35% (FIRE, CASHCAT, PONS), 0.7% dynamic via LONG hook (AI, SPACEHOOD). AI/SPACEHOOD are quoted in tokenized stocks (NVDA, SPCX): extra hop each way. Pons V2 hook has 100 bps hook fee + up to 10% creator tax; none of the 15 tokens is V2 but any future universe would hit it. | On-chain `fee()`, decoded v4 Swap `fee` field, `readpons.py` | +1 pp round trip for 9 tokens, +1-1.5 pp for AI/SPACEHOOD (9 events). |
| M4 | **TP/SL "median +11.8%" is mechanically uninformative and reproduces under random entries.** Any rule that hits +15% more than 50% of the time has median ~ +15% - cost. Permutation null 95th pct of median = +11.7% vs observed +11.8%. Only the mean carries information (+6.4% vs null [-5.2%, +2.7%], p<0.001 on claim set) and it depends on wick fills: 22/49 TP hits (45%) closed below +15%. Stops are not level-filled on-chain: FIRE 07-20 triggered -30.4%, next swap -40.3%. | `audit_grid.py`, `audit_null2.py`, `exec_audit.json` | Drop the median figure. Realistic TP/SL mean after fixes: +1% to +4%, tail loss per stop -33% to -40%. |
| M5 | **Missing 4h/24h exits silently dropped.** 10/65 24h returns missing in the core set (15%); 62/293 in the refreshed set (26 right-censored, 36 candle gaps = no trades for >= 15 min after a crash). | Claim 24h +24.6% (n=55). Missing = -100%: median +6.1% (65-set), -2.0% (299-set), -3.3% to -10.3% in other treatments. Next-available fill: +14% to +23%. | 24h median lies between -2% and +14% depending on treatment; +22.8% is not defensible. |
| M6 | **Statistics do not survive clustering or multiple testing.** 65 events = 43 independent 24h clusters, 15 tokens, 2 tokens = 23 events; token-clustered 95% CI of net 1h median [-0.2%, +10.8%], 4h [-1.4%, +15.0%]; token-level sign test 10/15 (p=0.15). Core combo is one cell of a ~360-cell grid (208/246 cells positive; best-of-grid 24h +66%); 48 `rep()` subset reports plus 1m variant and two extra universes. Claim mean does not beat max-of-grid null at any close-exit horizon. ## 2. Corrected expectancy after applying every valid fix

Fixes applied: drop SPACEHOOD artifacts (M1); event-time liquidity proxy instead of current liq (F1); per-pool fees 2 x (0.5% + pool fee) + stock hop where relevant (M3); impact = size / measured event-time depth (M2); TP/SL fills at first swap after trigger, not at level (M4); 60s reaction latency (M7); token-clustered CIs (M6). F2 cannot be fixed from the data, so every number below is still an **upper bound** on the true universe.

| Exit rule, $500 clip, automated 60s reaction | Median | Mean | % positive | Tail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1h close (75 min) | +1.5% to +3.4% | +2.6% to +4.5% | 55-61% | worst events -30% to -40% |
| 4h close | 0% to +0.6% | ~0% to +7% (outlier-driven) | 50% | same |
| 24h close | undefined: -2% (missing = -100%) to +14% (next-available fill) | outlier-driven (3 trades supply most of it) | 48-62% | dead tokens not counted |
| TP +15% / SL -30% / 4h | +6.7% to +9.2% (mechanical, ignore) | **+1% to +5%; central ~+3%** | 77-82% hit | stopped trades fill at -33% to -40%, not -30% |

Token-clustered CI on the TP/SL mean without the current-liquidity lookahead: roughly **[0%, +3%]**. Post-claim events (n=15): mean -3.6%. Aug+ subset with measured impact: 1h median -5.0%.

Sensitivity that kills it:

- **Clip size:** $2,000 -> TP/SL median +2.9%, mean -0.4%; $5,000 -> median -7.7%, mean -12%, 36% positive.
- **Reaction time:** 5 min -> $500 mean +3.2%, $2k mean -2.6%; 15 min (manual) -> most of the bounce is gone, net ~ -2%.
- **Activity regime:** depth/3 -> $500 mean +1.5% (Aug+ +0.9%); $2k median -11% to -17%.
- **Universe:** hindsight-free Solana set -> all horizons negative, TP/SL mean -5.7%.
- **Concentration:** only liq >= $500k (n=19, July-heavy) is clearly positive (1h +8%, 79%); worth, LIGER, FIRE, YOLO per-token 1h net are negative under measured impact.

Blunt summary: a $500 automated clip on the same 3-4 surviving tokens made about +3% mean per trade in July-August with a heavy left tail; everything larger, slower, later, or on a universe chosen without hindsight is zero or negative.

## 3. Minimum changes to make this live-safe (i.e. not lose money on known defects)

1. **Never filter or cost on `pools_v3.json` `liq`.** Use event-time depth: on-chain pool reserves / V3-V4 `sqrtPrice` and `L` at the signal block, or empirical $ per 1% from the last N swaps. Require depth >= ~$1,000 per 1% move at signal time.
2. **Fix the universe rule up front and freeze it.** Universe = tokens that meet the depth rule at signal time, on Robinhood chain only (Solana shows nothing). Do not use "traded by today's leaderboard" as an input; act24 adds nothing and is hindsight-contaminated.
3. **Reject implausible candles.** Skip any token whose GT pool has `base=False` or a non-WETH/USDG quote (AI, SPACEHOOD class); require |return| <= k x volume/depth and >= 20 swaps in the crash candle; confirm the crash from swap logs before entering.
4. **Cost model:** fees = 2 x (0.5% app + actual pool fee) + any hop, read `creatorTaxBps`/`hookFeeBps` from the Pons V2 hook before touching a V2 token; impact = clip / measured depth, both legs. Skip if projected round trip > 4%.
5. **Size:** cap at $500 per event (<= 2% of measured depth), no averaging down.
6. **Execution:** automated poller only, entry within 120s of the 15m candle close; abort if price already > +2% above crash close at fill time. Manual trading on the fomo app is not viable (no price-drop alerts, 15 min reaction removes the edge).
7. **Exits:** treat TP and SL as market orders at next observable price with impact; model stop fills at -35% not -30%; a gas guard for direct on-chain (skip when baseFee > ~2 gwei on a $500 clip).
8. **Drop the 24h hold and the "median" reporting.** Pre-register one rule (TP15/SL30/4h or 1h close) and score it on the mean and the sum of P&L, with token-clustered CIs.

## 4. What paper trading still has to verify (cannot be settled from the backtest)

- **Does the bounce exist on a universe chosen without hindsight?** Run the frozen rule from item 2 forward on every qualifying token, including ones that die. This is the F2 test; the only hindsight-free data so far is negative.
- **Realised fill vs signal:** actual entry price vs crash close at +60/120s, and actual TP/SL fills vs trigger levels (gap size on stops).
- **Realised round-trip cost** per pool (app fee + pool fee + hook/creator tax + impact) versus the 3-4% assumption; breakeven for the swap-verified median is 4.7%.
- **Capacity:** whether a $500 clip itself moves these pools 2-4% one-way as the depth measurements imply, and whether repeated clips degrade.
- **Regime:** July-August activity may have been the peak; measure depth and event frequency weekly. A 3x drop in depth turns the $500 clip to ~+1% mean.
- **Tail control:** frequency and depth of -30%+ stops and dead-token events over >= 60 independent events (one per token per 24h), not 65 overlapping ones.
- **Post-claim drift:** the 15 events after Sep 3 were negative; need >= 100 clustered events before any positive mean is believable at the 95% level.

---

## 5. Overall verdict

**Not a real, retail-executable edge.**

- The claimed numbers (+6.5% 1h, +22.8% 24h, TP/SL +11.8% median) are not reproducible (+4.8% from the saved file), are built on a filter that uses September liquidity to pick July trades, on a universe of the 10% of socially-active tokens that survived, on two fabricated candle winners, and on a cost model that understates impact by 4-6x and fees by 1 pp.
- Once those are corrected the short-horizon (15-75 min) median is 0% to +2% and the token-clustered CIs include zero; the 24h and 4h results are grid-selection noise on right-skewed tokens; the only honest out-of-sample tests (post-claim events, hindsight-free universe, Solana) are flat to negative.
- What is real is a generic AMM overreaction bounce of +2% to +4% in the 15 minutes after any -15% candle, symmetric with pumps and unrelated to leaderboard activity. It is of the same size as the true round-trip cost, is gone within 5-15 minutes, and exceeds costs only for an automated bot trading ~$500 per event on a handful of deep pools during an active regime. That is a capacity-limited scalp worth perhaps a few hundred dollars a week at best, not a retail strategy, and it has not yet been shown to work on any universe selected without hindsight.

Recommendation: do not trade it as described. If pursued at all, rebuild as the automated $500-clip rule in section 3 and treat the forward paper-trading results in section 4 as the first real evidence; the current backtest provides none.
